notes.text: John Marino is out week to week (upper body injury) and has missed the last 5 games. He is a top-pair defenseman. Andrew Peeke has taken his spot beside Nate Schmidt.
Michael Carcone is on injured reserve and has missed the last 9 games. Jack McBain has taken his spot beside Kevin Stenlund and Daniil But.
Nick Suzuki is out (upper-body injury) and has missed the last 4 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Oliver Kapanen has taken his spot beside Cole Caufield and Juraj Slafkovský.
Ivan Demidov is on injured reserve (lower-body injury) and has missed the last 11 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters.
Mike Matheson is day to day (lower-body injury) and missed their last game. He is a top-four defenseman. Lane Hutson has taken his spot beside Noah Dobson.
Owen Beck was added to the roster on Oct 23 and has played beside Jake Evans and Kirby Dach.
Oliver Kapanen is no longer killing penalties: 0% of the team’s shorthanded time in 6 games, down from 33% last season.
Arber Xhekaj has started killing penalties: on the ice for 28% of the team’s shorthanded time in 12 games, up from 6% last season.

stakes: The Mammoth go in second in the Central with 18 points, the Canadiens tied for second in the Atlantic with 18 points.

MTL.head: The Canadiens face a real test
MTL.body: Utah has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately, while Montréal will be without Suzuki. Then again, Utah will be without Marino, and Montréal has home-ice advantage. The Canadiens’ best way through is getting good looks.

UTA.head: The Mammoth have a lot going for them

story.head: The Canadiens are rolling
paras: The Canadiens have won four straight, and the Mammoth (9-5-0) beat Pittsburgh 4-3 in overtime on Oct 29. Going in, the Mammoth are second in the Central (tied for sixth in the NHL) and the Habs second in the Atlantic (tied for sixth).

The Mammoth have played better than their record (.643) says: their chances are worth about .737, and their goaltending has held them back. The Canadiens’ record (.692) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.567), largely thanks to pulling off wins in one-goal games.

The Mammoth roll their lines more evenly than anyone (1st), rarely get pinned in their own end (1st) and let the point shots come and guard the net (2nd). As for the Canadiens, they get into more chippy games than almost anyone (3rd), take more penalties than they draw (32nd) and give up a lot of dangerous shots (29th). Something has to give when the Mammoth’s shooting runs into the Canadiens’ defense, and the Mammoth have the edge over the Canadiens on the power play.

Clayton Keller (4 G / 12 A / 16 P in 14 GP) leads the Mammoth in scoring. Logan Cooley (7 G / 8 A / 15 P in 14 GP) has a team-high seven goals, with seven points in his last five games. For the Canadiens, Cole Caufield (8 G / 4 A / 12 P in 13 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Lane Hutson (3 G / 8 A / 11 P in 13 GP) is next in line.
Karel Vejmelka (6-4-0 / .877 SV% in 10 GS) is in line to start for Utah. Jacob Fowler (6-1-0 / .942 SV% in 7 GS) has been outstanding for Montréal and will likely start.
